scenes.title: TWO CLOCKS. ONE DECISION.
scenes.narration: What should a system do when its market clock and quote timestamps do not agree? Pause. Today's paper-only cycle could not reconcile those time references, so no entry was authorized.

scenes.title: TIME IS PART OF THE DATA
scenes.overlay: Every quote needs a reliable timestamp.
scenes.narration: A price without a trustworthy time is incomplete evidence. The market clock, quote time and bar interval must make sense together before a system can act.

scenes.title: CHECK COMPLETED BARS
scenes.overlay: A partial candle is not final evidence.
scenes.narration: A candle can keep changing until its interval ends. Confirm the session, compare timestamps and use completed bars only. Never guess.

scenes.title: FILTERS MUST AGREE
scenes.narration: A strong-looking chart cannot override weak liquidity, a wide spread or missing confirmation. A ranking is a research priority, not permission to enter.

scenes.title: NO TRADE IS VALID
scenes.overlay: Do not guess to keep moving.
scenes.narration: When the time references conflict, pause, record the reason and resume only when the data can be trusted. No trade is a valid result.

scenes.title: VERIFY. THEN DECIDE.
scenes.narration: AMORDER: verify the clock, verify the data, then decide. Paper-trading education only; not live-money performance; not investment advice; no guaranteed returns.

Two clocks disagree? Pause. A quote without a trustworthy timestamp is incomplete evidence. Check the session, compare the time references and use completed bars. If the data cannot be reconciled, stop instead of guessing.
